subject.title: [Feature]: Intent-scoped MCP activation for large MCP catalogs

question: Should request-scoped MCP activation be owned by the generic embedded-run tool policy, with persistent configuration defining only the eligible upper bound?
rationale: The performance gap and implementation surface are clear, but choosing a separate MCP selector without a canonical owner would create overlapping policy and ambiguous precedence with the recently centralized request allowlist.

options.title: Extend generic run policy
options.body: Represent all, none, or named MCP servers in the channel-agnostic run tool policy and filter before catalog work.

options.title: Add a separate MCP selector
options.body: Introduce a dedicated closed selector and explicitly define its precedence against the existing request tool policy.

options.title: Retain full activation
options.body: Decline subset activation and rely only on parallel cataloging, caching, runtime sharing, or separate agents.

recommendation.title: Extend generic run policy
recommendation.body: Represent all, none, or named MCP servers in the channel-agnostic run tool policy and filter before catalog work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal covers the MCP catalog lifecycle where the selected policy must be enforced safely.
